audit.why: 49.33% Emerald+ over a lane Sett owns from level 1 to two items. The 8/10 lane rating is honest: he is resourceless, out-autos Kassadin with Pit Grit and Knuckle Down, and his level 6 is a genuine execute pattern while Kassadin's level 6 is only an escape.

audit.whatIsWrong: All seven stages read Sett, including Two+ items — whose own caption says 'Riftwalk stacking plus Rabadon's/Lich Bane lets you blink around his slow, dash-less kit, dodge Facebreaker, and burst him before he charges W'. full.phases[6] carried the same contradiction under a why reading 'The monster is awake... Hunt.'
audit.why: Sett has no dash and no scaling; the content layer, the full layer and the late-game text all say the 2+ item window belongs to Kassadin. Only the side label disagreed. The six earlier stages genuinely are Sett's and are unchanged.
audit.corrected: Two+ items to Kassadin on win[6] and phases[6].side.

audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker's actual rule was never stated. Riot: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' The page called it 'the E pull-stun' everywhere and only gestured at positioning with 'stay off the line between him and units'. Whether you get stunned or merely slowed is entirely a positioning choice, and slowed is survivable while stunned into a charged Haymaker is not. Second gap: Haymaker's Grit loop is half-told. Riot: 'Sett passively stores damage he takes as Grit. On cast, Sett expends all stored Grit to gain a shield and punch an area, dealing true damage in the center and physical damage on the sides.' The pages mention the true-damage core but never that poking him is what loads it, and never that it also gives him a shield your burst has to chew through. Third: Knuckle Down is never named on either layer.
audit.why: All three come straight out of Riot's ability text, and together they invert the instinctive play — do not chip a Sett, and do not stand opposite a minion.
audit.corrected: The both-sides stun rule is now in wants.foe[0], wants.you[0], dosFull[0], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5]. The Grit loop is in whys[1], whys[2], late, dosFull[1].t and breakdown.cooldowns, including the shield. Knuckle Down is named in whys[1]. Haymaker's side-versus-centre split is in spikes[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d called it a 'fifteen-second invitation' and no other field gave a number.
audit.why: Facebreaker is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s. Sixteen at rank 1, and since Sett pays no resource the cooldown is the only thing limiting how often he can commit.
audit.corrected: 16s at rank 1 down to 10s is now in mid, winCon, dosFull[0], dosFull[2], breakdown.cooldowns and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer says to trade and 'walk out as the shield absorbs his counter', dosFull[1].t says 'Q-shield right before his trade lands', and report[6] says 'Fleet plus Q shield is how you survive'. breakdown.late claims a 'Q-silence'.
audit.why: Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic damage only; Sett's Haymaker core is true damage and everything else in his kit is physical. The content layer already states this correctly, so the two layers contradicted each other. Null Sphere has no silence.
audit.corrected: Shield claims replaced with the true-damage reality; silence replaced with the interrupt.

edits.before: Through 4-5 your Nether Blade mana restore and maxed Q let you farm under tower, but this is still survival, not a fight window — Sett wins the all-in on raw grit. Level 6 is HIS spike here, not yours: E Facebreaker into charged W into R suppress can chain-kill you before your first Riftwalk charge or Q shield resets, so hold R purely as an escape to blink out of his pull range, never as engage. Bait the Facebreaker — once it whiffs he has no gap-closer, so step in for a Q, then back off on its cooldown.
edits.after: Through 4-5 your Nether Blade mana restore and maxed Q let you farm under tower, but this is still survival, not a fight window — Sett wins the all-in on raw grit. Level 6 is HIS spike here, not yours: Facebreaker into a charged Haymaker into The Show Stopper can chain-kill you before your first Riftwalk resets, so hold R purely as the escape from his 490-range pull, never as engage. Bait Facebreaker — 16s at rank 1 — and once it whiffs he has no gap-closer at all, so step in for a Q and leave on its cooldown.

edits.before: This is the only phase you own, and it is why you suffer everything before it. Once Riftwalk is stacking off Rabadon's and Lich Bane, Sett's slow, dash-less kit cannot land Facebreaker on a target that blinks every couple seconds — you bait the W charge, dodge the pull, and burst him with Q into stacked Riftwalk. Note his damage is physical and true, so your Void Stone magic reduction does little here; you win on mobility and burst, not on tanking him. Reach this window alive and you flip the lane completely — he has no answer to blink-spam once you out-scale his grit.
edits.after: This is the only phase you own, and it is why you suffer everything before it. Once Riftwalk is stacking off Rabadon's and Lich Bane, Sett's slow, dash-less kit cannot land Facebreaker on a target that blinks every couple seconds — you bait the pull, dodge it, and burst him with Q into stacked Riftwalk. Two caveats: his damage is physical and true, so Void Stone's magic reduction does little, and Haymaker hands him a shield built out of the Grit your own poke fed him — so open only once his W is spent. Reach this window alive and you flip the lane completely.

Also unresolved: full.diff is 'EVEN' while diffRating is 8/10, breakdown.difficulty says 'Hard matchup' and tone is the red #ff5d6c. Same inconsistency as the Renekton file.
